original_question: Suppose a polynomial p in two variables over C has smooth, irreducible, rational zero set. Must p be a factor of a field generator, equivalently, does there exist a polynomial q such that the generic fiber of pq is rational?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.1, with the paper’s explicit equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2; Theorem 1.3 is the adjacent local context that should be checked before sharpening the wording.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient setting (a polynomial in two variables over C), the correct geometric hypothesis (the zero locus is smooth, irreducible, and rational), the intended conclusion (being a factor of a field generator), and the paper-faithful equivalent reformulation via multiplying by another polynomial so that the resulting map has rational general fiber. The later literature uses exactly this field-generator/rational-polynomial dictionary over C. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
missing_details: State the ambient ring explicitly as C[x,y] and the affine curve as V(p) ⊂ A^2_C. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
Define “field generator”: F ∈ C[x,y] is a field generator if there exists G ∈ C(x,y) with C(F,G)=C(x,y). ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))

Define “p is a factor of a field generator” explicitly: there exists h ∈ C[x,y] such that ph is a field generator. The paper’s equivalent reformulation replaces h by q and asks that pq be a rational polynomial. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))

Spell out what “the generic fiber of pq is rational” means in this context: for general λ ∈ C (equivalently, the generic fiber over C(pq)), the affine curve pq=λ is rational; over C this is the same language as saying pq is a rational polynomial. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))

Make clear that the hypothesis concerns the affine zero fiber p=0 itself, not the projective closure or an arbitrary member of the pencil. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
It helps to say that “rational” means the curve has function field C(t), i.e. its normalization is P^1_C. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
Add the nonconstant/nonnull condition on p, even though it is implicit from the curve hypothesis. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
refined_question: Let p ∈ C[x,y] be a nonconstant polynomial such that the affine plane curve V(p) ⊂ A^2_C is smooth, irreducible, and rational. Must p divide some field generator of C[x,y]; that is, must there exist h ∈ C[x,y] and G ∈ C(x,y) such that C(ph,G)=C(x,y)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (Proposition 1.2), given p ∈ C[x,y] with V(p) smooth, irreducible, and rational, does there exist q ∈ C[x,y] such that pq is a rational polynomial, i.e. such that the morphism A^2_C → A^1_C defined by pq has rational generic fiber (equivalently, for general λ ∈ C, the curve pq=λ is rational)?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s opening conjecture about whether one smooth irreducible rational affine fiber already forces divisibility by a field generator. The q-formulation should be kept only because the paper itself gives that equivalence in Proposition 1.2; it should not replace the conjecture by a broader classification problem. The nearby context matters because, over C, the paper is working in the established equivalence between rational polynomials and field generators, and Theorem 1.3 is a proved neighboring case rather than a replacement for the conjecture. ([aix1.uottawa.ca](https://aix1.uottawa.ca/~ddaigle/articles/RatPols.pdf))
